absent: Lock ordering among su_mutex, dentry locks, and inode or parent locks, plus sleeping versus atomic contexts.
RCU and sequence-lock retry protocol for concurrent dentry lookup, including memory ordering.
Name hash algorithm, comparison semantics for encrypted or case-folded names, and QSTR_INIT definition.
Enabled debugfs implementations behind the disabled fallbacks, including file lifetime and cancellation.
Quota disk layout, free-space allocation, and transaction handling beyond credit constants and depth formula.
FDPIC loading, address assignment, and stack or map creation from elf_fdpic_params.
Definitions and behavior of d_is_reg, __d_entry_type, and other helpers referenced but not routed here.
Dentry lifecycle transitions for aliasing, splicing, shrinking, and RCU freeing, including d_move and d_splice_alias.

findings.text: Item callbacks use release to free the item, allow_link to authorize a new association between a source and a target, and drop_link to observe removal of such an association.

Group callbacks use make_item to create a child item from a parent and name, and make_group to create a child subgroup similarly. Member disconnect_notify reports detachment of a child, while drop_item releases it. Predicates is_visible and is_bin_visible decide per-index visibility of ordinary and binary attributes for an item.
Subsystem state pairs su_group storage with su_mutex protection. Helper to_configfs_subsystem maps a group pointer to its enclosing subsystem, returning null for null input.

The subsystem mutex serializes operations on the embedded group. A helper whose name marks it as already protected simply forwards to the general dependency-release routine, so callers must already hold the required protection and the helper itself adds no locking.

Descriptor qstr pairs hash and len values with a name pointer to unsigned bytes. The pair shares storage with combined view hash_len through a nested union. Declaration helper HASH_LEN_DECLARE has two orders swapping hash and len. Constructor QSTR_LEN builds a value from a pointer and length.

Entry header carries d_flags guarded by the entry lock, plus d_seq for optimistic protection, d_hash for lookup chaining, and d_parent linkage. Naming uses overlapping views with public d_name, while d_inode points at the target or stays empty for negatives. Short storage d_shortname holds inline bytes.

Later fields carry d_op hooks, d_sb ownership, d_time for revalidation, and d_fsdata private data. Combined object d_lockref joins lock with count apart from lookup data. Linkage uses d_lru for recency, d_sib for sibling position, and d_children for descendants. The tail union exclusively selects d_alias for positives, d_in_lookup_hash for in-lookup negatives, d_rcu for deferred freeing, or waiters for shrink races.

Flag protection relies on alias d_lock for the entry spinlock. Locking classes distinguish DENTRY_D_LOCK_NORMAL for plain acquisition from DENTRY_D_LOCK_NESTED for nested use. Sequence and reference machinery stays separate from lookup-touched fields.

Validation hooks use d_revalidate for full checks and d_weak_revalidate for lightweight checks. Name handling uses d_hash for hashing and d_compare for comparison. Lifecycle hooks use d_delete to vote on removal, d_init to initialize, d_release to free, d_prune to discard, and d_iput to release the inode binding.

Naming hook d_dname renders into a caller buffer. Traversal hooks use d_automount to supply mounts and d_manage to control transit. Stacking hook d_real selects the underlying entry guided by D_REAL_DATA versus D_REAL_METADATA. Alias coordination uses d_unalias_trylock to attempt locking and d_unalias_unlock to release.

The hash marker DCACHE_OP_HASH uses bit 0. The compare marker DCACHE_OP_COMPARE uses bit 1. The revalidate marker DCACHE_OP_REVALIDATE uses bit 2. The delete marker DCACHE_OP_DELETE uses bit 3. The prune marker DCACHE_OP_PRUNE uses bit 4. Disconnection DCACHE_DISCONNECTED uses bit 5. Recent use DCACHE_REFERENCED uses bit 6. Purge on release DCACHE_DONTCACHE uses bit 7. Mount veto DCACHE_CANT_MOUNT uses bit 8. Waiter presence DCACHE_LOOKUP_WAITERS uses bit 9. Shrink membership DCACHE_SHRINK_LIST uses bit 10. Weak revalidation DCACHE_OP_WEAK_REVALIDATE uses bit 11.

Silly-renamed state DCACHE_NFSFS_RENAMED uses bit 12. Watched-parent state DCACHE_FSNOTIFY_PARENT_WATCHED uses bit 13. Killed state DCACHE_DENTRY_KILLED uses bit 14. Mountpoint DCACHE_MOUNTED uses bit 15. Automount need DCACHE_NEED_AUTOMOUNT uses bit 16. Transit management DCACHE_MANAGE_TRANSIT uses bit 17. Least-recent-use membership DCACHE_LRU_LIST uses bit 18. The combined mask DCACHE_MANAGED_DENTRY unites the mountpoint, automount-need, and transit-management bits.

The type field DCACHE_ENTRY_TYPE spans bits 19 through 21. Value 0 DCACHE_MISS_TYPE means negative miss. Value 1 DCACHE_WHITEOUT_TYPE means whiteout. Value 2 DCACHE_DIRECTORY_TYPE means directory. Value 3 DCACHE_AUTODIR_TYPE means lookupless automount directory. Value 4 DCACHE_REGULAR_TYPE means regular file. Value 5 DCACHE_SPECIAL_TYPE means other special. Value 6 DCACHE_SYMLINK_TYPE means symlink. Higher markers use bit 22 for DCACHE_NOKEY_NAME, bit 23 for DCACHE_OP_REAL, bit 24 for DCACHE_PAR_LOOKUP, bit 25 for DCACHE_DENTRY_CURSOR, bit 26 for DCACHE_NORCU, and bit 27 for DCACHE_PERSISTENT.

Entry kind behaves as an exclusive state drawn from miss, whiteout, directory, lookupless automount directory, regular, special, and symlink. Whiteout halts traversal while lookupless directories presume automount without lookup. Helpers d_is_whiteout and d_is_special test their respective states, while d_is_file combines d_is_reg with d_is_special.

The capacity macro DNAME_INLINE_WORDS has three alternatives: 5 with 192 bytes, 9 with 128 bytes, and 11 with 128 bytes. Total length DNAME_INLINE_LEN multiplies the word count by machine word size. The union shortname_store overlays a byte string with a word array of that capacity. The alias d_iname exposes the byte view, while d_lock aliases the entry spinlock.
Accessor d_count reports the count held in d_lockref. Predicates d_is_whiteout and d_is_special test their respective kinds, while d_is_file combines d_is_reg with d_is_special.
Snapshot name_snapshot stores a name descriptor copy in name alongside private inline_name storage for the bytes.

Wrapper debugfs_blob_wrapper pairs data pointer with size. Descriptor debugfs_reg32 pairs name with offset. Set debugfs_regset32 combines regs array with nregs count, base mapping, and dev pointer for power management. Array debugfs_u32_array pairs array pointer with n_elements count.

Table debugfs_short_fops offers read, write, and llseek. Callback type debugfs_automount_t maps an entry and data to a mount. Cancellation instance debugfs_cancellation links through list and stores cancel callback with cancel_data.

Base macro DEFINE_DEBUGFS_ATTRIBUTE_XSIGNED builds an open handler plus operation table from get, set, format, and signedness inputs. The open step validates the format then uses a shared attribute opener. The table wires release with shared read and selects signed versus unsigned write handling. Wrappers DEFINE_DEBUGFS_ATTRIBUTE and DEFINE_DEBUGFS_ATTRIBUTE_SIGNED fix the signedness to false and true respectively.

Helper debugfs_create_file_aux selects debugfs_create_file_full for file-operation tables and debugfs_create_file_short for short tables, for both constant and mutable pointers. Numeric helper debugfs_create_file_aux_num encodes a number into the auxiliary pointer, while debugfs_get_aux_num decodes it via debugfs_get_aux.

Disabled lookup debugfs_lookup and auxiliary creation debugfs_create_file_aux report missing-device failure. Unsafe creation debugfs_create_file_unsafe plus directory, symlink, and automount creators debugfs_create_dir, debugfs_create_symlink, and debugfs_create_automount do the same, while sized creation debugfs_create_file_size with removals debugfs_remove, debugfs_remove_recursive, and debugfs_lookup_and_remove do nothing. The recursive alias names the plain removal.

Disabled transfer helpers debugfs_attr_read, debugfs_attr_write, and debugfs_attr_write_signed report missing-device failure. Boolean and string helpers debugfs_read_file_bool, debugfs_write_file_bool, and debugfs_read_file_str do the same, as does debugfs_change_name for renaming.

Disabled creators debugfs_create_u8, debugfs_create_u16, debugfs_create_u32, debugfs_create_u64, debugfs_create_ulong, debugfs_create_x8, debugfs_create_x16, debugfs_create_x32, debugfs_create_x64, debugfs_create_size_t, debugfs_create_atomic_t, debugfs_create_bool, debugfs_create_str, debugfs_create_regset32, debugfs_create_u32_array, and debugfs_create_devm_seqfile do nothing. Companion helpers report debugfs_create_blob as missing-device failure, debugfs_print_regs32 as no-op, debugfs_initialized as false, debugfs_file_get as success, and debugfs_file_put as no-op. Helper debugfs_create_xul delegates to 32-bit or 64-bit handling by width of unsigned long.

Format table qtree_fmt_operations offers mem2disk_dqblk for memory-to-disk conversion, disk2mem_dqblk for the reverse, and is_id to test ownership. Control block qtree_mem_dqinfo records dqi_sb owner, dqi_type kind, dqi_blocks total, dqi_free_blk and dqi_free_entry hints, dqi_blocksize_bits exponent, dqi_entry_size length, dqi_usable_bs capacity, dqi_qtree_depth precomputation, and dqi_ops table pointer.
Helper qtree_depth derives fanout by quartering dqi_usable_bs, then expands coverage multiplicatively until spanning the 32-bit identifier space, counting levels from one.

Generic tree credits use QTREE_INIT_ALLOC 4 with QTREE_INIT_REWRITE 2 for creation, and QTREE_DEL_ALLOC 0 with QTREE_DEL_REWRITE 6 for deletion. First-version credits use V1_INIT_ALLOC 1 with V1_INIT_REWRITE 1 for creation, and V1_DEL_ALLOC 0 with V1_DEL_REWRITE 2 for deletion. Second-version symbols V2_INIT_ALLOC, V2_INIT_REWRITE, V2_DEL_ALLOC, and V2_DEL_REWRITE reuse the corresponding generic tree values.

Parameters elf_fdpic_params bundle hdr copy with phdrs table pointer and loadmap pointer, plus addresses elfhdr_addr, ph_addr, map_addr, and entry_addr, alongside stack_size request, dynamic_addr and load_addr bases, and flags word.

Arrangement mask ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_ARRANGEMENT is 0x0000000f. Within it, ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_INDEPENDENT is 0x00000000, ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_HONOURVADDR is 0x00000001, ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_CONSTDISP is 0x00000002, and ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_CONTIGUOUS is 0x00000003. Stack and object bits use ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_EXEC_STACK 0x00000010, ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_NOEXEC_STACK 0x00000020, ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_EXECUTABLE 0x00000040, and ELF_FDPIC_FLAG_PRESENT 0x80000000. Generic names Elf_Sword, elf_fdpic_loadseg, elf_fdpic_loadmap, and ELF_FDPIC_LOADMAP_VERSION map to Elf32_Sword, elf32_fdpic_loadseg, elf32_fdpic_loadmap, and ELF32_FDPIC_LOADMAP_VERSION in one case and to Elf64_Sxword, elf64_fdpic_loadseg, elf64_fdpic_loadmap, and ELF64_FDPIC_LOADMAP_VERSION in the other. Property alignment uses ELF32_GNU_PROPERTY_ALIGN 4 and ELF64_GNU_PROPERTY_ALIGN 8.

A null d_inode marks a negative and must not be dereferenced. An entry flagged DCACHE_DISCONNECTED may be detached with a self or similarly flagged parent and needs lookup-time splicing via d_move or d_splice_alias before server use. Flags DCACHE_NFSFS_RENAMED, DCACHE_DENTRY_KILLED, DCACHE_PAR_LOOKUP, and DCACHE_LOOKUP_WAITERS plus the waiters list coordinate deletion, invalidation, and concurrent lookup waits.

Disabled-mode failure encodings must be tested with error-pointer checks rather than null checks, since creation and lookup return a failure value instead of null. Silent no-op removals and creators can hide absence of the feature, and trivial acquire success does not imply a usable backing object.

Headers publish cross-file interfaces: config item and group callback tables with subsystem embedding, name and entry descriptors with operation hooks and flag vocabulary, debug creation and typed helpers, quota conversion and control descriptors, and loader parameter blocks.

Each header defines its own inclusion sentinel: __LINUX_DCACHE_H for name cache, _DEBUGFS_H_ for debug entries, _LINUX_DQBLK_QTREE_H for quota trees, _LINUX_DQBLK_V1_H and _LINUX_DQBLK_V2_H for quota versions, _LINUX_ELF_FDPIC_H for position-independent executables, _ELF_RANDOMIZE_H for randomization, and _LINUX_ELF_H for executable format. The compatibility marker compat_brk_randomized is defined empty in both of its alternative configurations.
External error-pointer constructor owned by another dossier and relied upon by disabled debug helpers to report missing-device failure.
External container lookup owned by another dossier and relied upon to recover a subsystem from its embedded group.
